<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5945f1c5079b916072959bbc83f83369499b6d6d` — the merge of head `64b2202b1193426637be611228778390ff89de38` into base `fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5945f1c5079b916072959bbc83f83369499b6d6d && git checkout 5945f1c5079b916072959bbc83f83369499b6d6d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450 64b2202b1193426637be611228778390ff89de38 && git checkout -B drift-repro fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450 && git merge --no-ff 64b2202b1193426637be611228778390ff89de38

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `64b2202b1193426637be611228778390ff89de38`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line on the changeset and the PR body is true and complete against the diff. New in `scorecard.ts`: export `repeatTally`, type `QuestionRepeats`, optional `HalfScores.repeats` and `CardScorecard.askRepeats`. New in `orchestrate.ts`: optional `RunOptions.askRepeats`, `QuestionResult.repeat`, `CardRun.askRepeats` (outside the strict `counts`, so the exporter's record parse still passes), and an optional seventh `runHalf` parameter defaulting to 1. New in `driver.ts`: optional `StepRef.repeat` and `RecordedDriver.heldAsks` / `assertAskRepeats`. All reach `./runner` through `export *`. The new CLI flag `--ask-repeats N` (whole number above 0, default 1) is not live-only: under `recorded:` it sets how many recorded asks are read, and a count the recording does not hold for any question turn is refused before any card runs.

The answer that moves is declared and is confined to N > 1. `stepKey` returns today's key for an absent or first repeat and adds `/repeat-N` only for asks 2..N, so every existing recording replays (seat read: `RecordingDriver` and `RecordedDriver` key by `stepKey(task)`, and the task now carries `repeat`). With N = 1 no result carries `repeat`, the card run carries no `askRepeats`, the scorecard has no k/N table and the heading is unchanged; the thread pins that byte for byte through the runner and through the gallery exporter. Operations run once. A seed-dependent turn is not measured at every ask. Guardrails, `Run · model`, `Ask cost` and `Ask time` count each ask as a turn. `buildTranscript` carries each result's `repeat` into its `StepRef` (claim amendment 6897633587), so an N > 1 record joins each ask to its own reply.

### ② Semver level

Patch, as the changeset bumps it. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no spec key, app metadata or card JSON changes. The widening is additive exports, optional fields and one optional parameter of the evaluation package `@objectstack/scenarios`. No existing export is removed, renamed or narrowed. `stepKey` now throws on a `repeat` below 1 or not whole, a value no caller could pass before the field existed.

### ③ Boundary flags

None. No `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path, no platform runtime or security behaviour. No grader verdict moves: each ask is graded by the unchanged `gradeCardAnswer`, and the scorecard only counts what the record carries.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-esnefl`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qiby1cctpVpRbJzjccvY`

**VERDICT: PASS**
